thread:
Mira Chen: Quick heads-up — noticed ~10–30ms host-side tail on small-chat workloads after the kernel-selection tweak landed. Looks correlated with gRPC streaming requests where seq len is 256-512.
Alex Park: I saw that on staging canary this morning too. Tail is much worse when batch sizes are small. :eyes:
Jordan Li: can you paste the pprof flame or a short trace? guessing extra memcpys in parse/tokenizer path or an extra syscall per chunk.
Mira Chen: pasted a tiny capture below (captured during a controlled ramp):
```
# pprof top (host preparse)
12.3ms  parse_shim::deserialize
8.7ms   tokenizer::tokenize_batch
6.4ms   net::writev
4.1ms   kvcache::lookup (miss)
3.2ms   grpc::frame_align
```
Stack trace shows repeated writev for small chunks (>1 syscall per message).
Sam O'Neill: writev storm often from streaming chunking sending many tiny frames. We recently changed framing to flush-on-boundary in kernel hint path — might be the trigger.
Jordan Li: also kvcache misses are interesting — are we fragmenting keys per chunk? a per-chunk shard key would bust locality.
Mira Chen: confirmed: fragment-level keying introduced in PR #4217. KV hit-rate drops ~12% on these traces.
Tariq Siddiq: that's consistent with the latency spike — KV miss triggers disk fallback in the dedicated path occasionally (slow path), adding jitter.
Alex Park: quick experiment idea: gate new kernel selection so it only wins when (batch_size >= 8 || seq_len >= 1024). For small batches keep previous codepath. That should avoid the tiny-frame pressure.
Jordan Li: agree. Also two more small wins: 1) coalesce grpc frames client-side into a single writev per request when possible; 2) revert per-chunk kv keying to prefix-based key (keep fragment id out of shard key).
Mira Chen: can someone prototype the writev coalescing? it's a minimal change in ingress framing layer.
Sam O'Neill: I can take a look. If we can build a cheap buffer in the host proxy and send one syscall per response it should drop syscall overhead.
Hailey (ci-bot): CI: build/test for refs/pull/4238/merge queued — runs: unit, integration, perf-smoke.
Alex Park: perf-smoke should include a 1k-conversation microbench covering 256/512/1024 sequences. Need a before/after to validate tail improvement.
Jordan Li: also add KV hit-rate metric to perf-smoke (prefix vs fragment key). We need to see eviction behavior.
Mira Chen: added two logs from the failing run: small http/gRPC header sizes + many tiny frames, and a readout of KV hit ratio (staging): hit 78% -> 66% after PR.
Sam O'Neill: quick patch idea: in host-framer, buffer up to 16KB or until end-of-response, whichever first. Should not increase latency for typical small responses but will reduce syscalls.
Tariq Siddiq: keep an eye on memory pressure if many concurrent streams buffer; suggest per-connection cap and global token bucket for mem usage.
Alex Park: plan: (1) Sam prototypes writev coalescing + per-connection cap (PR from Sam), (2) Jordan prepares gate for kernel-selection heuristic (PR from Jordan), (3) Mira reverts KV keying to prefix and adds test for hit-rate (PR from Mira). Target: land in staging Canary tomorrow.
Mira Chen: assigning owners in thread: Sam -> writev coalesce, Jordan -> kernel gate heuristic, Mira -> kvkey revert + tests. I’ll coordinate the perf-smoke run.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: staging-canary-2026-03-20T09:00Z -> started. build: 4230.
Alex Park: once PRs are up, tag me. I'll run the microbench and share before/after graphs. :thumbsup:
Jordan Li: we should also consider a long-term fix: make kernel selection take into account expected framing cost (estimating syscall count) and kvcache locality score. Short term gate is fine.
Mira Chen: agreed. For now the conservative gate should mitigate user-facing tail. Thanks all — will post results from the perf-smoke run here.
Sam O'Neill: starting prototype now.
Hailey (ci-bot): CI: perf-smoke run for refs/heads/jordan/kernel-gate started (job id 9123).
Mira Chen: action items summarized: Sam (writev coalesce + caps), Jordan (kernel gate), Mira (kv revert + hit-rate tests), Alex (run perf benchmarks + compare), Tariq (monitorKV slow-path alerts during canary).
Jordan Li: timeline: PRs today, staging canary tomorrow, promote if tail reduces by >= 50% on 95/99p.
Mira Chen: thanks — I'll update this thread with numbers. :rocket:
